item.title: 2027-01-15 to 2027-01-17 — Tales & Legends with the Lancaster Symphony Orchestra
item.description:
Engagements: 2027-01-15 to 2027-01-17

Location: Gardner Theatre at Lancaster Country Day School,725 Hamilton Road, Lancaster, PA 17603, USA

Price: Not supplied by this calendar; check event details

Music's greatest storytellers take center stage in a program dedicated to the art of musical narrative. Wagner's grand Prelude to Die Meistersinger opens with themes of mastery and tradition, followed by the world premiere of Austin Wintory's Interactive Concerto for Guitar featuring 4-time Grammy-nominated guitarist Mak Grgić in an innovative new work that bridges classical and contemporary worlds. The concert concludes with Rimsky-Korsakov's enchanting Scheherazade—the ultimate musical storyteller—spinning tales from the Arabian Nights with exotic melodies, shimmering orchestration, and the seductive voice of the solo violin. From European legends to interactive innovation to Arabian tales, this concert celebrates music's timeless power to tell extraordinary stories.

item.description:

Location: Manheim Township Library, MTP Morgan Center B, 595 Granite Run Drive, Lancaster, PA, 17601

Price: Free

Grab a piping-hot mug of authentic colonial coffee and step right into the high-stakes winter of 1776! Join living historian Samuel Leamer to uncover the bold strategy, hidden Lancaster County connections, and dramatic reality behind Washington’s famous crossing of the Delaware and the epic 1st Battle of Trenton. Separate fact from fiction, sip historical brews, and discover how coffee and courage helped turn the tide of the Revolutionary War! Registration is encouraged A Berks County native and Cairn University history graduate, Sam Leamer has spent a lifetime bringing the past to life through reenactments-- and a decade mastering the art of modern coffee. By blending historical scholarship with coffee expertise, Sam offers a richer, deeper look into Colonial Coffee Culture, showing how the humble coffee bean helped fuel America’s fight for independence.

ASL Interpretation: Certified interpreters for select performances provide American Sign Language interpretation. If you need to cancel your reservation, contact access@thefulton.org so that we may extend an offer to wait-listed patrons. The Pay-What-You-Want program is available for patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing at all ASL interpreted performances. Audio Description is a carefully timed narration of the onstage visual elements in the performance, including the action, costumes, and scenery. Program notes via headset are available 10 to 15 minutes before show time, and a touch tour may be available 1 hour before the show depending on the production (details will be sent via e-mail if a touch tour is available and a separate no-cost reservation will be required). Patrons may pick up their receiver and headset, free-of-charge, at Audience Services, located in the coat room on the right side of the main lobby. Open-Captioned performances provide patrons with live text presentation of onstage dialogue on a LED screen situated in a box to the right side of the stage. The captions seen on the LED screen may be read from most seats in the theatre, though many prefer seats in the Parquet or Orchestra sections for the best view. An experienced captioner scrolls text in sync with the actors’ spoken word. Tickets can be reserved at the box office or online. Join us for an educational and inspiring puppet play that explores the stories of immigrant families in New York City—plus, free kids' activities and crafts!
